sources.title: François Golse, The Mean-Field Limit for the Dynamics of Large Particle Systems, Journées Équations aux dérivées partielles short course (2003), complete 23-page course
sources.locator: Full 23-page PDF retrieved and stamped. Read Sec. 1.1.1 (printed pp. 1–3), Sec. 1.2.1 (pp. 6–7), Part I §§I.1–I.6 (PDF pp. 12–15), and Appendices I.A–I.B (pp. 16–22) including the complete Dobrushin coupling and chaotic-sequence arguments. The unrelated quantum Parts II–III are not claimed as read.

contents.name: Sec. 1.1.1 and Part I: the Vlasov equation, classical N-body Hamiltonian and Liouville equation under 1/N scaling
contents.support: The source distinguishes exact N-body Hamiltonian motion from mean-field evolution, states the 1/N weak-coupling scaling, and writes the empirical-force average and Liouville equation. The local definition gives the narrower periodic-potential model, SI dimensions and hypotheses; no Coulomb or unbounded-force assumption is imported.

contents.name: Sec. 1.2.1 and Part I: finite-particle Hamiltonian and Liouville transport
contents.support: The course supplies the finite-particle Liouville starting equation, not the exact BBGKY marginal calculation. The assigned proof derives every normalized k and N-k coefficient locally by integration by parts and permutation symmetry, retaining correlations.

contents.name: Appendix I.A: Dobrushin stability for a first-order mean-field characteristic equation and empirical measures
contents.support: The course proves the first-order estimate with exponent 2 Lip(K) t and applies it to empirical measures. The assigned second-order phase-space proof is derived separately with the streaming term and the stated exponent (1+2A)|s|; the course's first-order constant is not substituted.

contents.name: Appendix I.B: chaotic sequences, empirical-measure convergence and fixed-marginal propagation of chaos
contents.support: The course proves the symmetric-chaotic-sequence equivalence and propagates chaos for iid data in its first-order Lipschitz model. The assigned proof supplies the compact-support empirical W1 bounds and the finite-k with-replacement comparison directly for the periodic second-order model.

contents.name: Other quantum, singular-force, fluid-vorticity, Boltzmann and long-time topics in the course
contents.reason: These discussions use quantum, singular-force, fluid or collision-scaling hypotheses absent from this assigned smooth periodic finite-N model and do not prove any additional item promised by this pair.

contents.name: Sec. 1.1.1 and Part I: Vlasov characteristic equation and smooth interaction regime
contents.support: The course states the Vlasov characteristic formulation. The assigned theorem proves global existence, uniqueness, weak transport and the all-moment smooth-density branch locally for the narrower smooth periodic force.

contents.name: Part I: adopted weak-coupling particle preparation and mean-field comparison
contents.support: The course supplies the classical 1/N particle model and mean-field preparation context. The postulate records the narrower even periodic model, compact iid branch, full Choice use for an infinite sequence, and explicit non-empirical status.

contents.name: Sec. 1.2.1: global finite-particle Hamiltonian flow and Liouville transport
contents.support: The course gives the finite-particle Hamiltonian and Liouville equation. The assigned proof adds complete-flow, permutation symmetry and rapid-tail conclusions directly for the smooth bounded periodic force.

contents.name: Appendix I.A: phase-space W1 coupling-cost definition
contents.support: The appendix defines the coupling infimum used for W1. The local definition supplies the periodic position metric, velocity moment domain, and finiteness without assuming an optimal coupling.

contents.name: Part I: finite-N correlations and the exact hierarchy comparison
contents.support: The course supplies the Liouville starting equation; the local proof derives every normalized marginal coefficient by periodic integration by parts and symmetry, without importing a closure or factorization.

contents.name: Part I: initially factorized finite-particle law as an illustrative case
contents.support: The source provides the exact interacting Liouville dynamics. The assigned N=2 Gaussian example computes the marginal and joint time derivatives locally and proves immediate loss of product structure.

contents.name: Appendix I.B: weak-* topology for measure-valued particle data
contents.support: The course defines weak-* measure convergence by compactly supported continuous tests. The local A-page lemma proves the exact smooth-test determination needed for its weak and density arguments from dominated convergence and Dynkin, without importing a source proof.

sources.title: Pierre-Emmanuel Jabin and Zhenfu Wang, Mean Field Limit and Propagation of Chaos for Vlasov Systems with Bounded Forces (2015), complete 37-page paper
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF retrieved and stamped. Read §§1.1–1.4 (printed pp. 3–16), including the Liouville and Vlasov weak–strong formulations, Theorem 2 hypotheses and Theorem 3 proof route; read §§2.1–2.2 (pp. 19–28) for the complete combinatorial estimate and Appendix 3 (pp. 29–33) for Theorem 1/Proposition 2. The separate §1.5 discussion is not used.

contents.name: Sections 1.1–1.2: the 1/N Newton system, weak Liouville formulation and Vlasov weak–strong uniqueness
contents.support: The paper independently presents the deterministic 1/N particle system and its Liouville/Vlasov formulation. Its bounded rough force, density and weak–strong hypotheses differ from the locally proved smooth periodic characteristic result.

contents.name: Sections 1.3–1.4 and 2.1–2.2: relative-entropy propagation of chaos and the combinatorial moment estimates
contents.reason: The paper's theorem requires a smooth limit with exponential velocity-gradient control, finite initial entropy and moment bounds, and proves L1 marginal convergence by a distinct relative-entropy/combinatorics argument. The assigned compact-support iid/Wasserstein proof does not invoke those hypotheses or estimate.

contents.name: Stochastic diffusion variants, rough-force existence without a unique particle flow, and the short-time strong-density regularity branch
contents.reason: The assigned pair is deterministic and has a smooth periodic force with a unique complete particle flow; it neither uses the paper's degenerate diffusion nor claims its rough-force entropy or Vlasov-Poisson regimes.

contents.name: Sections 1.1-1.2: bounded-force Vlasov weak equation and characteristic comparison
contents.support: The paper independently treats the particle and Vlasov formulations. Its rough-force, density and weak-strong assumptions differ; the assigned proof supplies a separate smooth periodic characteristic argument.

contents.name: Section 1.1: deterministic 1/N particle model and iid initial preparation
contents.support: The paper corroborates the deterministic N^-1 particle scaling. The local postulate spells out the selected periodic interaction and compact iid preparation rather than importing an entropy or Vlasov-Poisson assumption.

sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140 (American Mathematical Society, 2012), 356-page textbook
sources.locator: Read Chapter 2 §2.2, printed pp. 36-40 (basic existence and uniqueness); §2.4, pp. 42-48 (dependence on initial data; Theorem 2.10 assumes joint C^k regularity in time and state); and §2.6, pp. 50-53 (extensibility). The local A-page lemma proves the exact continuous-time/smooth-state jet conclusion used here rather than importing stronger time-regularity hypotheses.

contents.name: Chapter 2: the basic existence and uniqueness theorem, dependence on initial data, and extensibility
contents.support: The textbook supplies the local Picard existence, uniqueness, continuation and initial-data dependence background. The assigned lemma proves the needed state-jet conclusion for a field continuous in time and smooth only in state, with its exact hypotheses and differentiated integral equations.

contents.name: Other perturbation, linear-system, boundary-value and dynamical-systems chapters
contents.reason: No parameter perturbation, boundary-value, spectral or long-time stability claim from those chapters is used by the assigned bounded-force characteristic construction.

note: Coverage is source-anchored. The current batch-30 manifest and draft A page contain def-csm-dk-hamiltonian-flow-measure; its exact definition was inspected, and batch-31 consumers use its canonical phase convention while retaining its draft status. Every theorem claim remains a local conditional argument; the lecture-note treatment and independent bounded-force paper have different hypotheses and methods.
